paragraphs: (1) He is bar Yosef bar Hama: Eruvin 54a; Sukkah 34, end of a; Hullin 43b. In Bava Metzia 70a, ‘Rabbah bar Yosef bar Hama’ is a scribal error and should read Rava. He was not a priest, and received priestly gifts on account of his wife, Rav Hisda's daughter. I do not know where he found that Rava received priestly gifts on account of his wife. Without argument or proof he decided an issue disputed by Tosafot and Rashi. For Rosh Hashanah 18a says: ‘Rava and Abaye came from the house of Eli. Rava, who occupied himself with Torah, lived forty years; Abaye, who occupied himself with Torah and acts of kindness, lived sixty years.’ Rashi explains: ‘In Ha-Zeroa we find that Rava was not a priest; perhaps his mother came from Eli's house’ (below I shall write an objection to this). ‘Some read Rabbah and Abaye; this is Rabbah bar Nahmani’ [רבא בר נחמני in source]. End quotation. In Ha-Zeroa, 133a, Rava told his attendant, ‘Acquire the gifts for me.’ (Rashi explains: although Rava was also a priest, since he descended from Eli's family, and in Bekhorot 27 he used to nullify terumah from outside the Land in a majority and eat it in his impurity, nevertheless he could not take for himself, for it says ‘he shall give,’ not that he should take himself. He did not wish to tell them to give him, so as not to ask for his portion with his mouth. He therefore took it as a non-priest would, through a priest's gift. Though it had not yet reached his attendant's hands, Rava relied on Rav Yosef's statement that even before it reaches a priest's hands, the priest may confer ownership.) Rava ate, but Rav Safra did not eat (because it had not reached the attendant's hands). They read to Rav Safra in a dream, ‘One who removes a garment,’ etc., ‘and sings songs to a troubled heart,’ Proverbs 25. (So is one who speaks Torah to someone unable to understand it—Rashi.) Rav Safra [סכרא in this occurrence] came before Rav Yosef and asked, ‘Perhaps because I transgressed the master's teaching’ (by not relying on your teaching that a Torah scholar may receive it even before it comes to a priest's hands) ‘they read this to me?’ He replied, ‘When I said it, I meant another’ (where a different priest, not subordinate to him, confers ownership; the householder's attendant is compelled to confer it on an important man visiting his employer's house). ‘And when I said it’ (alternatively: granted that I said a priest may confer gifts on another before they reach his own hands), ‘I meant someone unable’ (a poor, hard-pressed man); ‘but he is able’ (Rava is not in straitened circumstances). ‘Then why did they read this to me?’—since Rav Safra had not transgressed Rav Yosef's teaching. ‘With reference to Rava’—they read it to Rav Safra concerning Rava, who did not understand Rav Yosef's reasoning. ‘Then let them read it to Rava!’ ‘Rava was under rebuke.’ Rashi writes: ‘I heard that it was because he spoke defiantly toward Heaven in Ta'anit, asking for rain unnecessarily to honor King Shapur's mother’ (I shall copy the episode shortly). ‘In my view he was under rebuke because of this episode.’ End quotation. That is, he did not understand Rav Yosef's reasoning, and it was as if he ate forbidden food; therefore he was under rebuke. In Ta'anit 24b: Rava had a man flogged in court for intercourse with a gentile woman, and he died. King Shapur heard and wished to trouble Rava. Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur's mother, told her son, ‘Have no dealings with the Jews, for whatever they ask their Master, He does for them.’ He asked, ‘What is this?’ She answered, ‘They pray, and rain comes.’ He said, ‘That is because it is the rainy season. Let them pray now, in the summer solstice season, and let rain come.’ She sent to Rava—she was fond of Rava, Rashi explains—‘Concentrate and pray that rain come.’ He prayed, but rain did not come. He said, ‘Master of the world, with our ears we have heard, our fathers have told us, but with our eyes we have seen nothing. Now show us Your wonders!’ Rain came until the gutters of Mahoza poured into the Tigris. His father appeared to him in a dream and said, ‘Is there anyone who troubles Heaven so much? Rise and change your bed tonight, for Heaven is angry with you.’ He changed his place. The next day he found his bed scored with knives. (Demons had wished to kill him and slashed his bed. This is what we say in Ha-Zeroa, that Rava was under rebuke. We find no rebuke of him in the entire Talmud except this episode, when he asked for rain unnecessarily.) Here ends Rashi. In Ein Yaakov some of Rashi's words are missing, and there is a scribal error there. The Arukh, entry נזף, likewise writes this, as does Rif. But Rashi in the aforementioned Hullin passage introduces this explanation with ‘I heard,’ and writes, ‘In my view he was under rebuke because of the Hullin episode.’ Rosh on Hullin likewise explains: in the Ta'anit episode Rava was already presiding, since it occurred in his court; Rav Yosef had already died, for Abaye presided after Rav Yosef, and Rava after Abaye. Anyone who headed an academy was called ‘king,’ since he was a judge, as in Berakhot 62a: after Rava began presiding, his wife, Rav Hisda's daughter, made him a window and placed her hand upon him. How, then, could they have shown him in Rav Yosef's time that he was under rebuke? Necessarily he was under rebuke because of the aforementioned Hullin episode (see there). What follows is that according to Rashi he was a priest. Tosafot, Hullin there, write: ‘Rava told his attendant’—we read Rabbah, for Rava was a priest, as in Ad Kammah, where Rava nullified in a majority; we also say that Abaye and Rava descended from Eli's house. End quotation. Yet Tosafot, Bekhorot there, write: ‘Rava nullified’—we read Rabbah, who was a priest of Eli's house; Rava was not a priest, as is evident in Ha-Zeroa, ‘Rava told his attendant,’ etc. Tosafot, Yevamot 105a, likewise write this; see there at length. This is the opposite of what they wrote in Hullin. Necessarily there is a scribal error in Hullin; it should read: ‘Rava told his attendant’—we read Rava, for Rabbah was a priest, as found in Ad Kammah, ‘Rabbah nullified,’ as Tosafot themselves write in Ad Kammah, reading Rabbah. So too Tosafot, Menahot 67a: ‘Rabbah nullified.’ Thus according to Tosafot Rava was not a priest. This also appears to be Rashi's view in Rosh Hashanah there, where he writes that Rava was not a priest, as in Ha-Zeroa. Rashi's statements appear mutually contradictory. There would be some reason to think Rava was a priest, because in Hullin there Rav Yosef tested Rava: ‘A priest who snatches gifts—is he cherishing the commandment or treating it lightly?’ etc. It appears that he asked him because he was a priest. There is clear evidence that Rava was not a priest: Berakhot 48a says Abaye and Rava were sitting before Rabbah. Rabbah asked them, ‘Whom do we bless?’ They answered, ‘The Merciful One.’ ‘Where does the Merciful One dwell?’ Rava pointed toward the ceiling; Abaye went outside and pointed toward Heaven. Rabbah told them, ‘You will both be rabbis; gourds are recognized from their stems.’ End quotation. Thus Abaye and Rava were contemporaries and young, since he said ‘gourds.’ In truth, however, this needs examination. Pesahim 104b says that Rav Yehudah sent his son R' Yitzhak to see how Ulla recited havdalah (see there), and sent a basket of fruit with him. R' Yitzhak sent it by Abaye. Rav Yehudah was angry at his son and told him, ‘The master's authority and pride have caused him not to state a teaching from his own mouth’ (see there). Presumably Abaye was not a child when he was entrusted with the fruit basket and, moreover, with testimony about how Ulla recited havdalah. In the Jerusalem Talmud, R' Elazar bar R' Tzadok said, ‘I was a child riding on my father's shoulder and saw,’ etc. They told him, ‘You were a child, and a child has no testimony.’ When he saw the matter, he was no younger than ten, etc. (see above, R' Elazar bar R' Tzadok). Be that as it may, Abaye must then have been grown when Rav Yitzhak, sent by his father Rav Yehudah, sent him. Rava was born on the day Rav Yehudah died. How, then, could Abaye be a child and Rava's contemporary, even if Abaye's mission to Ulla was near Rav Yehudah's death? All the more if it was several years earlier: Abaye was plainly well advanced in years when Rav Yehudah died and Rava was born. Abaye lived sixty years, as above, and Rava presided fourteen years after Abaye's death, as הד״ע [provisionally Dorot Olam] and Yuhasin, Amoraim by Their Times, fourth generation, write; so too Rav Sherira Gaon's Epistle in Yuhasin. If he was Abaye's contemporary, he would have lived nearly seventy-four years. How, then, could Rosh Hashanah say Rava lived forty years? Necessarily the reading is ‘Rabbah lived forty years.’ Rashi's suggestion there that his mother came from Eli's family also raises the question: how did he live seventy-four years? Thus the correct reading is the one Rashi brings: Rabbah, namely Rabbah bar Nahmani. There is a terrible difficulty with Rashi's statement in Ha-Zeroa that Rava was a priest. One cannot say there is a scribal error in Hullin and read ‘Rabbah told his attendant, “Acquire the gifts for me,”’ so that Rashi accordingly wrote that Rabbah was a priest of Eli's house. This is necessarily impossible, since Rashi explains, ‘I heard that he was under rebuke because of the Ta'anit episode,’ in which he brought rain when Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur's mother, who frequently sent to Rava, sent to him—as I shall write below. Thus Hullin certainly reads ‘Rava told his attendant’; how could Rashi write that he was a priest descended from Eli's house?

(2) He was born on the day Rav Yehudah bar Yehezkel died: Kiddushin 72b. It therefore appears that in Bava Kamma 97, end of a, ‘Rava said to Rav Yehudah, “According to you,”’ is a scribal error; it should read ‘Rabbah said to Rav Yehudah.’ In Yoma 79a, ‘Rava said that Rav Yehudah said,’ and likewise in Jerusalem Talmud, end of Makkot chapter 2, there is no difficulty: we do find a person speaking in the name of someone he did not see, as I wrote in the introductory Rules. But ‘he said to him,’ as one speaking with him, is impossible. In Shabbat 129a, ‘Rav said in Rav Yehudah's name,’ it seems to me it should read Rava; so too in Tosafot. Shabbat 88: ‘Rav said, “Our affection still remains with us,”’ as in Ein Yaakov, should read Rava. So is that matter in Gittin 36, end of b, and Yalkut, Song of Songs. In Zevahim 45a Rava objected, ‘A halakhah for the messianic age?’ Tosafot, Yoma 13a, write that Rav Yosef raised this objection. Tosafot, Bekhorot 14a, write that Rava did not see Rav Huna (see there), who died before Rav Yehudah, while Rava was born when Rav Yehudah died (see Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzhak).
(3) His place was Mahoza. ‘Rava instituted in Mahoza’: Beitzah 30a; Rashi, Ha-Dar 63a, Ha-Zahav 59, end of a; Avodah Zarah 58, beginning of a; Niddah 67b. Tosafot, Gittin 60b, likewise write this.

(4) In Niddah 20b, Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur's mother, sent blood before Rav (it should read Rava). R' Ovadiah sat before him. Rava smelled it and told her, ‘It is blood of desire.’ (Rashi writes: although above Rava says he does not know blood, a miracle occurred for him. Tosafot write that Rava did know, and above they read Rabbah did not know. Rashi's statement that a miracle occurred applies only at the end, as is evident shortly.) She told her son, ‘Come see how wise the Jews are.’ He answered, ‘Perhaps like a blind man at a skylight.’ She then sent him sixty kinds of blood, and he identified them all. The last was blood of lice, and he did not know. Events assisted him: he sent them a comb that kills lice. She said, ‘The Jews dwell in the inner chambers of the heart.’ Yuhasin writes that R' Ovadiah smelled the blood; he erred (see there). In Bava Batra 10b, Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur's mother, sent four hundred purses of dinars before R' Ammi, who did not accept them; she sent them before Rava, who accepted them. In Zevahim 116b, Ifra Hormiz, King Shapur's mother, sent a calf to Rava, saying, ‘Offer it for the sake of Heaven.’ Rava told Rav Safra and Rav Aha bar Huna, etc., and they offered it for her for the sake of Heaven. In Hagigah 5b, the rabbis told Rava (Ein Yaakov has Rabbah, a scribal error), ‘The master is subject neither to hiding of the face nor to “it shall be for devouring,”’ etc. The rabbis set their eyes upon him; meanwhile King Shapur sent and plundered him. Rashi explains ‘they despoiled him’; the marginal explanation in Yalkut, end of Vayelekh, ‘they struck him,’ is erroneous. This is what was taught: wherever sages set their eyes, there is either death or poverty. End quotation. In Shevuot 6b, Rav Pappa asked Rava, ‘Which is superior, King Shapur or Caesar?’ He replied, ‘He eats in the forest’ [Rashi takes this to mean that Rav Pappa was unfamiliar with Rome’s power]. (Rashi explains: Rava was subject to King Shapur, as in Hagigah, ‘King Shapur sent and plundered him’; out of fear he named King Shapur first. End quotation.) Thus Ein Yaakov's reading Rabbah in Hagigah is a scribal error and should read Rava. In Pesahim 54, end of a, Rav Pappa called Rava ‘King Shapur.’ See above under shin, Shmuel, where I demonstrated that all the Persian kings were called King Shapur.

(5) He married Rav Hisda's daughter. Bava Batra 12b: since the Temple was destroyed, prophecy was given to children. For Rav Hisda's daughter sat in her father's lap, while Rava and Rami bar Hama sat before him. He asked her, ‘Which of them do you want?’ She answered, ‘Both.’ Rava said, ‘And I last.’ Hiddushei Aggadot writes that he did not curse Rami bar Hama to die before him, but meant that Rami bar Hama would divorce her and afterward Rava would marry her (see there). This too is evidence that Rava was not a priest, for how could he marry a divorced woman? In Yevamot 34, end of b, Rava told Rav Hisda's daughter, ‘The rabbis are murmuring about you’—R' Yohanan said that a woman who waits ten years after her husband and remarries no longer bears children, and she had waited after her first husband, Rami bar Hama. She told him, ‘My mind was on you,’ for Rav Nahman said that if her intention is to marry, she conceives. Tosafot write: Rabbenu Tam said this was because of the aforementioned Bava Batra episode, when she said, ‘I want both,’ and awaited fulfillment of her prophecy. Since Rava had another wife, she delayed marrying him, yet still awaited him. End quotation. In Shabbat 129a she immersed within thirty days of giving birth, caught cold, and they carried her bed after Rava to Pumbedita. See Rashi there: when her husband is not with her, she should not immerse within thirty days for purity purposes, since she is like a sick person. This gives some evidence that immersion at its appointed time is a commandment even when her husband is not in town, for purity purposes. In my work I discussed this at length and brought evidence from II Samuel 11, ‘She was purifying herself from her impurity’: Rashi, Radak, Ralbag, and Keli Yakar explain that she immersed from menstrual impurity (see there). Although Ein Yaakov, Helek 107, has ‘purifying herself from her impurity, and he had intercourse with her while she was menstruating,’ end quotation, there is certainly an omission here. Rashi in the Gemara says, ‘Purifying herself from her impurity: at that moment her impurity ceased, and he did not come,’ etc. Although I wrote a reconciliation of Ein Yaakov's reading in my homilies, this is not its place. Be that as it may, she immersed from menstrual impurity, yet her husband Uriyah was not at home but at war. Certainly according to Tosafot she was divorced—according to Rabbenu Tam, completely and unconditionally divorced. Even if her husband were suddenly to return, she would require seven clean days. What, then, was this immersion for? Necessarily immersion at its appointed time is a commandment even when her husband is not in town. Semag, folio 37, likewise writes in the Jerusalem Talmud's name that a woman may not remain in her impurity; his brother-in-law מהר״ש [name abbreviation unresolved] likewise directed his daughter to immerse even in winter when her husband was not in town. Rema, Yoreh De'ah, beginning of section 197, ruled oppositely; see Taz there, Tosafot, Yoma 8a at length, and Tosafot, Beitzah 18b. In Ketubbot 85a a woman came for judgment before Rava. At his wife's word he transferred the oath to her opponent. Rava said, ‘I know that Rav Hisda's daughter does not lie.’ He did not believe Rav Pappa, saying he did not know him sufficiently. This appears to give some support to what Tosafot write in Berakhot 62a: before Rava became head, when he went to the privy Rav Hisda's daughter rattled nuts for him; after he began presiding she made him a window and placed her hand upon his head. Tosafot write: ‘It is puzzling, for Rava necessarily did not begin presiding until after Abaye's death, as is evident above, 56, where bar Hadyah interpreted for him, “Abaye will die, and the academy will come to you.” So too at the end of Af Al Pi, 65a: Homa, Abaye's wife, came before Rava. This is puzzling, since above it appears that in his dream he saw her death before Abaye's death’—when bar Hadyah interpreted well for Abaye and badly for him, Rava said, ‘I forgive you everything except Rav Hisda's daughter.’ ‘One may answer: nevertheless she did not die until after Abaye.’ End quotation. According to the foregoing, when that woman came for judgment before Rava and he transferred the oath at Rav Hisda's daughter's word, Abaye had certainly already died: in Abaye's lifetime the woman would not have come before Rava, as Rosh wrote above concerning the man Rava flogged. It follows that she did not die until after Abaye.

(6) In Yoma 75b, Rava's tenant farmer used to bring him a kind of quail every day. One day he did not bring it. He heard a child saying, ‘I heard, and my belly trembled.’ He said, ‘Learn from this that Rav Hisda’—his father-in-law—‘has died; on account of the master’—for he was his teacher—‘the pupil ate.’ He asked three things of the Holy One, blessed be He: Rav Huna's wisdom (see there), and Rav Hisda's wealth, which were granted him; Rav bar Rav Huna's humility, which was not granted him: Mo'ed Katan 28a. In Sanhedrin 65, Rava created a man (through Sefer Yetzirah, from which they learned combinations of the Name's letters). He sent him to R' Zeira; the man would not answer him. R' Zeira told him, ‘You are from the associates; return to dust.’ In Eruvin 29a he said, ‘I am like ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias’ (see what I wrote under Abaye). In Yoma 76b, ‘Wine and fragrance made me discerning’; Rashi explains: made me discerning. His hands were battered and bleeding, but he did not know because of the depth of his concentration: chapter R' Akiva. Rava declared an ox belonging to the sons of bar (it seems to me it should read Rav) Ukva unfit. When it came before R' Abba, he said, ‘Tell Rav Yosef bar Hama's son’—Rava—‘to pay for the ox.’ Mar son of Ravina said, ‘We raise an objection against Rava's enemies’ [euphemistic wording]: Hullin 43b. In Nazir 53a: after Rava heard from R' Ukva. Tosafot write that this is the text in all the books, and it is not explained; perhaps it refers to Mar Ukva, who was in Rava's days. See Rav Akavya and Mar Ukva, where I wrote that it seems to me it should read ‘perhaps Rav Ukva, who was in Rava's days,’ namely, whose sons' ox he declared unfit. Rava said, ‘When I die, R' Hoshaya will come out to meet me, because I interpret the Mishnah in accordance with him’: Bava Kamma 111b; Bava Metzia 62, end of b. He said, ‘May I receive reward for this: when a Torah scholar comes before me for judgment, I do not lay my head upon the pillow until I have examined his side of the case’: Shabbat 119, beginning of a. He gave his hand to an elder so that he could rise before him (see Rav Nahman). Rava salted shibuta fish in honor of Shabbat: Shabbat 119a. He was careful about the commandment of tzitzit (see above, Rav Yosef bar Rava). Rava appointed a public expounder and declared, ‘Things I said before you were errors on my part’: Bava Batra 127, end of a; Niddah 68a; Eruvin 104a. He said, ‘May his Master forgive R' Tarfon’: Sukkah 32b. Rava became ill and said, ‘Why did I dispute the interpretation of the elders?’—Rav Yehudah and Rabbah bar Avuha—Shabbat 134b. Ravina asked Rav Pappa, ‘Were you not with us in the evening within the boundary at Bei Harmakh, where Rava set excellent teachings against one another and resolved them?’ Zevahim 2b. He told Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua and Rav Pappa: ‘When judicial documents come before you and you see an objection, do not tear them until you come before me.’ They are called ‘white geese’ (see there). He was serving drinks at his son's wedding. He lifted a cup for Rav Pappa and Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua, who rose before him; for Rav Mari and Rav Pinhas, Rav Hisda's sons, who did not rise before him, and Rava took offense: Kiddushin 32, beginning of b. Rav Safra told him, ‘Moshe, you have spoken well’: Shabbat 101b. Rashi explains: our teacher in his generation is like Moshe in his generation. In Sukkah 39, beginning of a, and Beitzah 38b, Rashi explains: he swore by Moshe's honor (see above, R' Hoshaya). Some explain: a great man like Moshe (see there). Ravin bar Rav Adda told Rava, ‘Your pupils say that Rav Amram said’: Menahot 7b; Zevahim 26b. Rashi explains ‘your pupils say’: your pupils said it in Rav Amram's name. In Yoma 50a he likewise told Rava, ‘Your pupils say that Rav Amram said.’ But in Zevahim 93, ‘he said to Rav’ should read ‘to Rava’; ‘your pupil said.’ In Mo'ed Katan 24a, ‘Ravin bar Adda told Rava, “Your pupil Rav Amram said”’ is a scribal error and should read as above. Yoma 50, end of a: Rava says that a jointly owned sin-offering is not left to die. It asks, ‘What difference does it make?’ and answers that the priests do not bring a bull for an erroneous ruling. Rashi explains that priests are not called a congregation. But this is difficult: in Horayot 6b Rava rejected Rav Aha's reasoning that anyone with a landed inheritance is called a congregation (Be'er Sheva, Horayot). See above, Ravina, where an unqualified Rava is bar Yitzhak. Rav Yosef challenged it; Abaye told him, etc.; Rava said, ‘This is what troubled Rav Yosef’: Pesahim 71a. Rav Nahman asked him to ask the Angel of Death not to distress him (see there).

(7) He lived twenty-eight years after Rav Yosef. This also appears so because Abaye presided after Rav Yosef for thirteen or fourteen years (see Part I), and Rava presided fourteen years: twenty-eight years. Responsa Ralbah, folio 294, column 4, writes that in their days there were courts called Sanhedrin, but they did not have the status of the Great Court and Sanhedrin. His brother Rav Se'oram persuaded the Angel of Death not to distress Rava (see there). When he died, the arches of the Tigris touched one another: Mo'ed Katan 25b. For his burial place, see Abaye. Yuhasin writes [Generations of the Amoraim, fourth generation] that he died in 4113. Responsa Ralbah, 290, end of column 4, likewise writes this, as does צ״ד [provisionally Tzeidah La-Derekh]. But Rav Sherira Gaon's Epistle in Yuhasin says he died in 663, which is 4111; so too Shenot Hayyim, Metzora, folio 123, column 3, and Sefer Keritut.

(8) His teachers: (a) His principal teacher was Rav Yosef. Hullin 133a: ‘Rav said, “Rav Yosef tested us”’ should read Rava. Yoma 53: when Rava took leave of Rav Yosef, he walked backward until his feet were struck and Rav Yosef's threshold was stained with blood. They told Rav Yosef—who was blind and did not perceive it—that Rava was doing this. He said, ‘May it be His will that your head be raised’—that you become head of the academy—‘above the whole city.’ See Responsa Sha’ar Efrayim, section 78. Rav Sherira Gaon writes in Yuhasin: ‘Although after Rav Hisda's death there was no gaon in Sura, Rava's authority was nevertheless much greater, and he exercised great rule’—over Pumbedita and Sura; Yuhasin after Rav Sherira Gaon's Epistle, in the account of the Sura academy's distinction. ‘Rav Yosef's blessing was fulfilled. Rava's years of presiding were fourteen, and throughout all Rava's years there was only one academy.’ End quotation. Abaye and Rava had academies during Rav Yosef's lifetime, as appears in the episode of Rav Dimi of Nehardea (see Rav Adda bar Ahavah) and in Ha-Zorek, Shabbat. Rav Yosef was angry with him, and he went to appease him on the eve of Yom Kippur: Yoma. In Nedarim 55a and Eruvin 54a, Rav Yosef recognized the cup Rava mixed for him. He said, ‘Do not sit on your feet until you explain to me,’ etc., ‘From the wilderness, a gift,’ etc. In Bava Metzia 60: ‘My mixing is well known.’ See above, Rav Yosef: he had wine that took two measures of water to one of wine; perhaps only Rava knew this. (b) Rav Hisda was his teacher—Rashi, Bava Metzia 40—and his father-in-law (see above, Rabbah); also Ha-Mefannin, Ketubbot, and the end of Berakhot. He and Rami bar Hama first learned the received text, then reasoning. ‘Rav Hisda said’: Eruvin 103b. (c) Rav Nahman was his teacher: Tosafot, Bava Batra 46b; Avodah Zarah 58a; Kiddushin 42b; Menahot 102a. He asked Rav Nahman: Shabbat 4, beginning of a, 70a, 91a; Eruvin 70, end of a; Yoma 61, end of b; Mo'ed Katan 13a. He challenged Rav Nahman: Bava Batra 39a. ‘Rav Nahman said’: Shabbat 91a; Nedarim 22b. In Rav Nahman's name: Eruvin 3, end of b. This needs examination: in Nazir 32a he tells Rav Nahman ‘according to you,’ without saying ‘master’; yet we do find that he called him ‘master.’ (d) R' Yohanan appears to have been his teacher, since Avodah Zarah 27b has ‘Rava said that R' Yohanan said,’ and Sanhedrin 104 has several statements. In Nedarim 59a Rav Hisda tells Rava, ‘Who listens to you and to your teacher R' Yohanan?’ In Shevuot 10b Rav Hisda tells Rabbah, ‘Who listens to you and to your teacher R' Yohanan?’ This needs examination: R' Yohanan died on the same day Rav Yehudah died (see above, Part I). It therefore appears that Nedarim should read ‘Rav Hisda told Rabbah,’ as in Shevuot. ‘R' Yohanan said’ in Avodah Zarah is no proof, as we find in the Rules. (e) R' Yitzhak bar Avdimi was his teacher (see there).

(9) The halakhah follows Rava because he is later: Tosafot, Berakhot 13b; Beitzah 9a; Shabbat 3a. There, 27b, Rava disagrees with Rav Nahman, and they rule like Rava because he is later. This disproves those who say that the halakhah does not follow Abaye and Rava against their teacher. ‘The halakhah follows Rava’ had to be stated concerning other amoraim, not concerning Abaye, since we hold that the halakhah follows Rava against Abaye except in Ya'AL KaGaM: Tosafot, Arvei Pesahim 103a; Tosafot, Mo'ed Katan 23, end of a. From Abaye and Rava onward, the halakhah follows the later authorities: see Kiddushin 45b, Tosafot beginning ‘An incident occurred’; Bava Batra 161a, Tosafot beginning ‘And it is necessary.’ Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 59, end of b: the halakhah does not follow Rav Pappa because Rava disagrees with him, although Rav Pappa is later than Rava, because Rava is his teacher, is also a later authority, and was greater in wisdom and number. In Tolin they ruled like Rava that one may wipe against a wall but not the ground. R' Zerahya Ha-Levi ruled like Rav Pappa because he is later; Ramban disagrees because Rava was Rav Pappa's teacher. In Rif, Ha-Mafkid: even if they disagree concerning Rabbah their teacher—see Rosh there; Responsa ש״א, section 133 [work unresolved]; Maharik, root 197, branch 2. Rosh, R' Eliezer De-Milah, rules like Rabbah because he is later than Rav. Elsewhere he writes that from Abaye onward the halakhah follows the later authorities, but not Abaye and Rava against Rabbah their teacher (see there). Yet at the beginning of Gid Ha-Nasheh he rules like Abaye against Rabbah, and at the beginning of Sukkah like Rava against Rabbah. In Ha-Maddir, section 13, Rosh is uncertain whether to rule like Abaye and Rava against Rabbah their teacher. The halakhah follows the teacher when he disputes his pupils during his lifetime; when they disagree after his death, the halakhah follows the later authorities (Ran, beginning of Sukkah), except R' Akiva against R' Eliezer his teacher, as found in Keitzad Mevarkhin, because the latter inclines to Beit Shammai's view (see R' Akiva, halakhic ruling). Rashba writes: ‘Rav Nahman was Rava's teacher, yet whenever Rava was not sitting before Rav Nahman, we hold like Rava. The sign is: where we find “Rava told Rav Nahman,” he is like a pupil sitting before his teacher, and we do not rule like him. When they disagree as two disputants generally do, the halakhah follows Rava.’ End quotation. See the introduction to Yuhasin. Ran, Gid Ha-Nasheh, writes that even where an amora acted against Rava's view, the halakhah follows Rava because he is more fully master of the Gemara. See Responsa Rosh Yosef, section 1: in Yesh Bekhor, R' Yirmeyah said, etc.; Rava said, etc.; we hold like Rava because he is more fully master of the Talmud than R' Yirmeyah and also later than him (see there). The halakhah follows him against Abaye (see there), except Ya'AL KaGaM. In Tzeidah La-Derekh, Mishpatim, ‘They pass the son on his legs,’ Re'em asks how Rashi ruled like Abaye rather than Rava. See Responsa Maharik, section 76, explaining Rashi differently. Rambam and ר״מ [authority abbreviation unresolved] likewise rule like Rashi. In my view, the rule that the halakhah follows Rava applies only when they disagree on their own authority—as Responsa Binyamin Ze'ev, section 63, also writes—not when they disagree concerning the opinion of another authority. End quotation. Perhaps the mem of KaGaM, according to Rashi, is Molekh. See Responsa Bah, section 55: the halakhah follows Rava against R' Hiyya bar Avin (see there), who was his pupil, for in Ein Bein Ha-Muddar, R' Hiyya bar Avin asked Rava (this needs examination; see there). See Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua: the halakhah follows him against Rav Huna, because he is later.

(10) Rava derives from the root of Naamah the Ammonite, Lot's daughter, and Rava emerged. This is the mystery of ‘They took Lot and his possessions, the son of Avram's brother’: the initials of ‘rekhusho ben ahi’ spell Rava. Likewise ‘Except only what the young men ate’: the initials of ‘bil'adai rak asher’ give the letters of Rava (Hesed Le-Avraham, spring 5, river 25). Avram's letters also spell ‘me-Rava’ (Kavvanot Ha-Ari, folio 50a). ‘Naamah the Ammonite, Lot's daughter’ means that she descended from Lot's daughters; she was Rehavam's mother. See Yevamot 77a: ‘Who are found for you’ means two finds, Ruth the Moabite and Naamah the Ammonite (see Bereshit Rabbah).

(11) R' Abba was in his time. R' Abba bar Zavda. Abba of Sura was in his time. Abba bar Marta, or bar Minyomi, went to console him [סזל in source]. In Abba bar Yirmeyah's name. R' Abba, Rav's father, in his name. Avuha bar Geniva sent, ‘Let our teacher instruct us.’ Abaye was his colleague and called Rava ‘master’: Ha-Ro'eh 61b. Abaye asked Rava: Mo'ed Katan 19b. Avimi of Hagronya in his name. Rav Adda bar Ahavah was his pupil. Adda Mari explained it to him. Adda the surveyor explained it to him. Adda Karhinai in his name. Rav Adda bar Mattana challenged him. Bar Ahina explained it to him. R' Avya. R' Hoshaya taught before him. Rav Aha bar Yaakov. Rav Aha of Difti spoke to him. R' Aha bar Bibi bar Abaye in his name. R' Aha bar Tahlifa in his name. R' Aha bar Adda was in his time. R' Aha bar Huna. R' Aha bar Abba spoke to him. R' Aha and Mar Zutra. Rav Aha was his son. Rav Aha bar Avira: needs examination. Idi explained it to him. Issur the convert. R' Iki bar Rav Ammi. Rav Iki bar Hanina. R' Iki of Parshunya raised a contradiction to him. R' Elazar of Hagronya. R' Elyakim was his attendant and pupil. Ammi spoke to him. R' Ammi, to whom Ifra Hormiz sent charity that he would not accept, whereas Rava accepted; ‘Ammi said.’ Amemar in his name. Rav Assi bar Hama spoke to him. Rav Ashi received from him, according to Rambam; in the Gemara, he was born when Rava died (see there). Binyamin the shepherd. Gurya bar Hama. Giddel bar Menashya: needs examination. Rav Gamda in his name. R' Dima bar Hama said. Rav Dimi bar Hinena before him. Rav Dimi, Rav Safra's brother, was in his time. Rav Huna in Rava's name: Shevuot 18a. It needs examination which Rav Huna this was, for Rav Huna died before Rava was born (see above). Rav Huna bar Hinena. Rav Huna bar Rav Yehoshua. Rav Huna bar Sehora. Rav Huna bar Mattana was in his time. Rav Huna bar Rav Nahman disagrees with him. Rav Huna bar Avin sent to him. Rav Huna bar Natan spoke to him. Rav Huna bar Tahlifa in his name. Rav Huna bar Manoah was his pupil. Rav Huna bar Yehudah. Rav Huna of Diskarta spoke to him. Hillel asked him. Rav Hamnuna was in his generation. Rav Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef. Ben Ha-Madori explained it to him. Rav Zevid in his name. R' Zeira called him ‘master.’ Ze'iri said. Rav Havivi was his son: needs examination. Rav Haviva son of Rav Yosef bar Rava in his name. R' Hizkiyah in his name. R' Hiyya taught before him. R' Hiyya bar Huna was his pupil. R' Hiyya bar Avin was his pupil (see above). He called R' Hiyya bar Abba ‘master.’ R' Hiyya of Vastini before him. R' Hiyya the Tall before him for judgment. R' Hinena bar Avin was his pupil: needs examination. Rav Hananya taught before him. R' Hama bar Buzi sat before him, and Rava called him ‘children’ (see there). Rav Hisda was his father-in-law and teacher. Hasa said. Rav Tuvya bar Kisna raised a contradiction to him. R' Yoshiya taught in Rava's academy. Rav Yehudah: when he died, Rava was born; ‘R' Yehudah said’ (see above). Yehudah bar Huna was in his time. Mar Yehudah; Rava called him ‘dissenter.’ R' Yehudah of Diskarta spoke to him. R' Yehudah bar Marimar in his name. Mar Yohana bar Rav Hana bar Adda, or son of Rav Hana bar Bizna: Rava happened to come to his house. R' Yohanan: whether he was his teacher, see above. A sage who had just arrived that day challenged Rava. He inspected an arrow for R' Yonah bar Tahlifa, and slaughtered a bird in flight. In R' Yannai's name: Jerusalem Talmud, Ketubbot chapter 1. Rav Yosef was his teacher. Also Rav Yosef bar Abba. Rav Yosef bar Hama was his father. Rav Yosef was his son. R' Yaakov, son of Shmuel's daughter, was in his time. R' Yaakov of Nehar Pekod in his name. R' Yaakov the sectarian challenged him. R' Yaakov bar Abba called him ‘master’ (see there). R' Yitzhak said. He spoke to R' Yitzhak son of רבב״ח [provisionally Rabbah bar bar Hana]. R' Yitzhak bar Avdimi was his teacher. R' Yirmeyah bar Abba said. R' Yirmeyah of Difti in his name. R' Yirmeyah said of his words, ‘Foolish Babylonians.’ Rav Kahana in his name: Bava Kamma 41, end of b. Rav Kahana, Rav Mesharshi's father-in-law, asked him. Minyomi bar Nahumi was in his time. Minyomi the physician spoke to him. Minyamin bar Hiyya was in his time. Minyamin כנדוקא [provisionally “the jar-dealer”] came before him. Mar bar Rav Ashi before him: needs examination. Mar bar Amemar in his name. Mar son of Rav Yosef in his name (see Mar son of Ravina). Rav Mordekhai asked him. Rav Mari bar Rav Hisda was his brother-in-law. Mari bar Issur the convert was in his time (see there). Rav Mesharshiya was his son. Rav Mesharshiya was his pupil. Nehardea in Rava's name. Rav Nehemya bar Yosef before him. Rav Nahman was his teacher. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak was his pupil. Rav Natan bar Ammi expounded before him. The elder of Pumbedita before him. Rav Sehora was his teacher. Rav Se'oram was his brother (see above). Rav Safra (see above). R' Ovadiah was his pupil. R' Avira in his name. Ulla appears to have been his teacher: needs examination. Ulla bar Rav asked him. Mar Ukva was in his time (see above). Rav Ukva bar Hama before him. Rav Ukva bar Hinena raised a contradiction to him. Rav Ilish before him. Rav Amram (see above). Rav Pinhas bar Rav Hisda was his brother-in-law. Rav Pinhas in his name. Rav Pappa was his pupil. Rav Pappa bar Hanan was his scribe. He spoke to Rav Pappa bar Shmuel. Rav Pappa bar Rav Aha bar Adda in his name. Rav Pappi in his name. Rava bar Mesharshiya spoke to him. Rabbah bar Sheila was in his time. Rabbah bar Levai challenged him. Rabbah bar Mattana. Rabbah was his teacher. He asked Rabbah bar Mari and happened to visit him. Rabbah bar Hanan bar Abba before him. He applied to Rabbi, ‘Drawing water from deep wells’: Shevuot 7, beginning of a. Ravin bar Rav Adda spoke to him. Ravin said. Ravin bar Rav Sheva explained it to him. Ravina called him ‘master.’ He called Ravina and R' Hama bar Buzi ‘children’ (see there). Ravina in his name: see there at length, where it appears one was his pupil and another preceded him. Rahva asked him. R' Rehumi before him. Rami bar Hama was his colleague. He called Rafram bar Pappa ‘master.’ Rav Sheva was in his time. R' Shimon the pious in his name. Rav Shimi of Nehardea. Rav Shimi bar Ashi in his name. Rav Shmuel bar Yehudah taught before him: needs examination. Rava arranged for Mar Shmuel to expound. Rav Shmuel bar Idi was his pupil. R' Shmuel bar Rav Sheva said. Also Rav Shmuel son of רבב״ח [provisionally Rabbah bar bar Hana]. ‘Shmuel said’: Nedarim 39, end of a. In Menahot 39, ‘in Shmuel's name’; in שס״ח, ‘Rabbah in Shmuel's name.’ He sent a message to Abaye through Rav Shemaya bar Ze'ira. Rav Sherevya in his name. Rav Sheshet said; and he spoke to Rav Sheshet. Rav Tahlifa, Rav Huna's father, in his name.
